note: Defines one-shot effects; instances are covered by other rules.

outcome: A one-shot effect that creates a delayed triggered ability makes it fire later instead of acting at resolution.
An until-effect moves the object, and a second one-shot effect returns it to its previous zone right after the specified event.
If the until-event already happened after the spell or activated ability went on the stack, the object does not move on resolution.
If the until-event already happened after the ability triggered, the object does not move on resolution.
An object returned to the battlefield by an until-effect enters under its owner control unless stated otherwise.
Return effects created after simultaneous events happen simultaneously, as with two exiled cards returning together.
A permanent phased out by an until-effect is phased back in by a second one-shot effect right after the specified event.
A permanent phased out this way does not phase in during its untap step, and if another effect phases it in the second effect does not happen.
If the until-event already happened after the spell or activated ability went on the stack, the permanent does not phase out.
If the until-event already happened after the ability triggered, the permanent does not phase out.
Phase-in effects created after simultaneous events happen simultaneously.
A static ability that grants a spell an ability as it is cast applies from the moment the spell is put on the stack.
